newsitem.title: USA: L.A. shootout robbers had been arrested in 93 - paper.
newsitem.headline: L.A. shootout robbers had been arrested in 93 - paper.

text.p: The two gunmen shot and killed by police in a gunbattle captured on live television had been arrested three years ago with a cache of assault-type weapons, bullet-proof vests and disguises, the Los Angeles Daily News reported Sunday.
But the men only served 71 days and 99 days in prison as a result of a plea-bargain, the newspaper said.

On Friday, the men identified by the Daily News and the Los Angeles Times as Larry Eugene Phillips and Emil Dechebal Matasareanu, were killed in a wild shootout in North Hollywood which was shown on live TV.

The Daily News said the indentifications came from suburban Glendale police. The Los Angeles police, 11 of whose officers were wounded in Friday's shooting spree after a botched bank robbery, has not named the two dead gunmen. Five civilians were also wounded in the gunbattle in which hundreds of rounds of armour-piercing bullets were fired by the robbers.
Police Chief Willie Williams said no details about the suspects would be released until homicide-robbery detectives and FBI agents had completed their investigations.

The FBI said Friday it believed the two gunmen, both of whom were seen firing at will with AK-47 rifles on police before being killed, were responsible for at least two prior bank robberies in the area.
The Daily News Sunday said the two were known as the "Shoot 'em Up Bandits," and had used automatic rifles in two bank robberies last year that netted them $1.5 million.
The newspaper quoted a deputy district attorney, James Grodin, as saying the men had been arrested in 1993 with a carload of high-powered weapons, ammunition, disguises and smoke bombs.
Grodin said authorities were frustrated they could not get conspiracy and robbery charges to stick against Phillips, 26, and Matasareanu, 30, at the time.
"We knew something smelled here. We knew they were up to no good," said Grodin. "I don't know if anyone is at fault for not following through."

As it was Phillips pleaded no-contest to one felony count and one misdemeanor count of weapons possession and was sentenced to 99 days in prison. Matasareanu served 71 days for admitting to weapons possession charges.
They also received 36 months probation in the plea-bargain, but all other charges against them were dropped in exchange for their pleas, the newspaper said.
